title: Hot-path allocation and over-broad event registration
cluster_summary: These are separate per-repo micro-costs with no shared root cause, so no upstream fix applies and each fix belongs in its own repo. Only CM-R-07 is worth doing: ConsumableMaster's OnSpecChanged ignores the unit argument, so a groupmate's respec triggers a full recompute and a SPEC_CHANGED broadcast. KickCD already filters this case, and copying its guard costs two lines. AT-R-02 and KC-R-09 are cheap, safe tidy-ups that can be done optionally. PFE-R-06 is mostly wrong because strings are interned and ApplyDriver already checks for equality. MM-R-09 is refuted as a defect: the behaviour is documented on purpose and the standard permits it.

verdicts.assessment: Confirmed: core/ConsumableMaster.lua:767 OnSpecChanged(event) has no unit filter. It runs requestRecompute and sends SPEC_CHANGED for every PLAYER_SPECIALIZATION_CHANGED, while KickCD Cooldowns.lua:695 already filters out non-player units. The fix is cheap and safe, and it removes a real recompute per groupmate respec.
verdicts.remediation: Change the signature to KCM:OnSpecChanged(event, unit) and add `if unit and unit ~= "player" then return end` as its first line. The guard must come before traceEvent, requestRecompute and the SPEC_CHANGED SendMessage, and must still let a nil unit through. Add an events test: a groupmate unit causes no recompute and no message, while 'player' and nil each cause one recompute and one message.

verdicts.assessment: Confirmed: modules/Timer.lua:40-42 builds a closure over painted/parent on every coalesced pass, which goes against the file's own hoisting rationale. The cost is negligible (one closure per pass, at most about 10 passes/s, and the ~1.4 KB/s figure was never measured). No test stubs ForEachUnit; tests/perf.lua only calls it.
verdicts.remediation: Optional: in doRepaint, replace the NS.ForEachUnit closure with `for _, unit in ipairs(NS.Units.LIST) do if NS.UpdateAbsorbBar(unit, parent) then painted = true end end`, the pattern core/AbsorbTracker.lua and core/Database.lua already use. No test changes are needed.

verdicts.assessment: Confirmed: core/Util.lua:190 allocates `{n=select('#',...), ...}` on every wrapped() call, including calls that coalesce. Cooldowns calls it with no arguments for SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN, SPELL_UPDATE_USABLE and SPELL_UPDATE_CHARGES. That is one tiny table per event in combat, which the incremental GC collects with no visible cost. A zero-arg sentinel is safe because fire() only reads args.n and unpack, and it does not break the guarantee that each burst keeps its own args.
verdicts.remediation: Optional: hoist `local EMPTY_ARGS = { n = 0 }` (never mutated) and set `pendingArgs = select('#', ...) == 0 and EMPTY_ARGS or { n = select('#', ...), ... }`. A perf scenario is not required for a two-line change that cannot alter behaviour. Add a unit test that a zero-arg throttle still fires fn once per burst.

verdicts.assessment: The driver-string half is refuted. Lua interns the short strings Driver builds, and ApplyDriver (UnitButtons.lua:58) returns early when __driverWant == driver, so an unchanged driver allocates no closure or key. What remains is one closure per in-combat secure Anchor.Apply (Anchor.lua:228). That path is rare and runs only on combat transitions, so caching it is not worth a perf scenario or extra state on secure code.

The facts are accurate, but nothing is wrong. events-frames-taint makes the private RegisterUnitEvent frame a MAY, docs/midnight-quirks.md and the code comments at core/MultiMeters.lua:155-159 document the choice as deliberate, the events are rare, and the reviewer recommends deferring too. Switching would add a frame that needs slash-commands-§7 teardown and mock coverage, with no measured benefit.
